analysis:
Examined docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: the only content change is the date bump (line 3) and a new paragraph at lines 670-690 describing the demandedLatestCheckpointRange scheduling behavior. It sets CBv2SchedulerConfig.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens to the store floor so a dense Qwen donor ends one range at the deepest aligned boundary at least 64 tokens below the prompt end. The text states that the fleet-novel refusal, first/target/latest retention, three-boundary limits, byte-admission limits and the store floor are unchanged. This documents a scheduling/capture-geometry change. It does not alter at-rest encryption (T-041 mitigations), HMAC lookup tags, TTL, cacheSalt tenant scoping or the authenticated restore path. Per the doc, cuts are made only for requests the store would write, so the donation-demand gating is preserved. It may slightly increase checkpoint writes for dense Qwen. These go through the same write budget and SSDCheckpointDemand admission, so I see no new data exposure. The TTFT oracle (SEC-035) is unchanged in kind.

The three submodule pointer bumps (libs/mlx, libs/mlx-swift, libs/mlx-swift-lm) show only commit hashes. The submodule diffs are not supplied, so the implementation behind the documented change, and any other changes in the native inference, KV cache, checkpoint codec and encryption paths (TB-007), cannot be assessed. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Integration should verify that the mlx-swift-lm bump 2beb401 implements the cut without bypassing cache-identity binding, the fleet-novel check or the byte/staging caps (CBv2HistoricalStagingCap). It should also confirm that no new unauthenticated restore paths or plaintext-at-rest artifacts were introduced. No findings are reportable on the supplied evidence; the review is flagged for deeper review because of the opaque dependency updates.
